title: Firm staff are auto-routed into a client-scoped app that dead-ends them
problem: A firm_staff user's very first sign-in lands them on a page whose main content is an unactionable dead end that gives them wrong advice, because the portal auto-redirects them to the SME app but firm principals have no client scope.
evidence: DEFAULT_WORKSPACE in artifacts/landing/src/App.tsx (lines 141-150) maps firm_staff to "/app/", and completeSignIn (lines 339-348) navigates there immediately after login without showing the workspace picker. But firm memberships carry clientPartyId: null (artifacts/api-server/src/bootstrap/seed.ts lines 550/557/722, Me schema in lib/api-spec/openapi.yaml line 6539), and the SME dashboard wraps its entire body in RequireClientScope (dashboard.tsx line 1632), which renders: "Your account isn't scoped to a client business, so there's no compliance summary to show here. Sign in with a client account." (require-client-scope.tsx lines 24-36). That instruction is wrong for a firm user — their account will never gain client scope — and the card offers no button, no link to the console, nothing. Every other core page (invoices/new, bills, vat, calendar, consent…) shows the same card.
fix: Two small frontend edits: (1) in artifacts/landing/src/App.tsx change DEFAULT_WORKSPACE.firm_staff to { href: "/console/", label: "Accountant Console" } so firm staff land where their portfolio work lives; (2) make RequireClientScope role-aware — when me.role is firm_admin/firm_staff, replace "Sign in with a client account" with "Open a client from the Accountant Console to work on their behalf" plus a Button (existing ui/button) linking to /console/. No backend change; the guard logic stays identical.

title: Session expiry hard-redirects to /login mid-task and never returns the user to where they were
problem: When the session cookie expires while a user is deep in the app, the next /me refetch (react-query's default refetchOnWindowFocus, e.g. returning from their authenticator or email tab) instantly executes window.location.href = "/login" with no warning, unmounting any open dialog or half-typed form; after re-authenticating, the portal always drops them at their workspace ROOT, never back at the invoice or page they were on.
evidence: sme-compliance require-session.tsx lines 107-110 and console require-session.tsx lines 113-116 both do `if (isError || !me) { window.location.href = PORTAL; return null; }` — a plain redirect with no returnTo parameter (grep for returnTo/redirect in artifacts/landing/src returns nothing). In the landing portal, completeSignIn (App.tsx lines 339-348) unconditionally navigates to DEFAULT_WORKSPACE[me.role].href, e.g. "/app/". So a user editing /app/invoices/:id who gets bounced must re-navigate from the dashboard by memory. Only invoice-new has a sessionStorage draft (invoice-new.tsx lines 235-242); dialogs like add-customer-dialog and reconciliation notes have none, so their in-progress text is destroyed silently.
fix: Frontend-only returnTo plumbing: in both RequireSession components redirect to `/login?returnTo=${encodeURIComponent(location.pathname + location.search)}`; in the portal's completeSignIn, read returnTo, accept it only when it is a same-origin relative path whose prefix (/app/, /console/, /buyer/) is allowed for the resolved role (reuse the APPS allowedRoles table already in App.tsx), else fall back to DEFAULT_WORKSPACE. Also show a one-line notice on the sign-in panel ("Your session expired — sign in to continue where you left off") when returnTo is present.

title: First-run dashboard congratulates instead of guiding a zero-data client
problem: A brand-new client with zero invoices lands on a screen that reads as 'all done': four zero metrics, a WorkQueue empty state saying 'Today is clear — there are no urgent submissions, failures or aged receivables', 'No recent activity', 'No upcoming deadlines', and a Month-end close card announcing 'All clear'. Nothing orients the user or tells them what the workspace is for; the only guided next step is a small inline text link buried inside the Receivables card's empty text.
evidence: dashboard.tsx: the today-view WorkQueue passes emptyTitle="Today is clear" (lines ~1680-1687); Recent activity and Next deadline cards render centered 'No recent activity' / 'No upcoming deadlines' text (lines ~1725-1729, ~1765-1769); the sole first-run CTA is showFirstInvoiceCta() rendering 'Create your first invoice' as an inline link inside ReceivablesCard's 'No outstanding receivables.' paragraph (lines 142-146, 221-240). The shared EmptyState component (empty-state.tsx) with an action slot exists but the dashboard never uses it.
fix: When summary.totalInvoices === 0, replace the WorkQueue with a first-run setup block: an EmptyState (existing component) titled 'Set up your compliance workspace' with two actions using existing Button+Link patterns — 'Create your first invoice' (/invoices/new) and 'Import existing invoices' (/import) — and keep 'Today is clear' only once at least one invoice exists. Pure conditional on data already fetched; no backend change.

title: Compliance tab renders a completely blank pane while its badge counts deadlines it never shows
problem: The dashboard's 'Compliance' segmented tab is populated exclusively by render-on-success cards: ClientStatementCard and AdvisoryBriefCard (both null unless the launch-dark Clerk statement/brief flags are lit and a document exists) and PenaltyExposureCard (null unless overdueCount > 0). On a fresh or healthy launch workspace all three return null, so clicking the tab shows nothing at all below the tab bar — no card, no empty state. Worse, the tab's count chip shows summary.upcomingDeadlineCount, but no deadline content exists anywhere in that tab (the Next deadline card is only mounted in the 'today' view), so a user clicks 'Compliance (2)' and finds empty space.
evidence: dashboard.tsx: the compliance view mounts only ClientStatementCard/AdvisoryBriefCard (lines 1796-1803, each 'if (!isSuccess || !x) return null' at lines 510, 555) and PenaltyExposureCard (line 1805-1807, returns null when overdueCount === 0 at line 1047). The tab item is { value: "compliance", label: "Compliance", count: summary?.upcomingDeadlineCount ?? 0 } (lines 1609-1613); SegmentedControl renders the count chip even for 0 (lib/web-ui/src/workspace.tsx lines 154-156). releases.ts confirms clerk flags are launch-dark.
fix: In the compliance view, mount the existing Next deadline card (so the badge has a referent) and add an EmptyState fallback ('Nothing needs compliance attention right now' with a 'View calendar' link) rendered when no advisory card has content — e.g. track presence via the same isSuccess data already fetched, or simply always render the deadline card plus the conditional cards.

title: 'Run with Clerk' button shows at launch though it can never succeed, and its error toast points at a card that does not exist
problem: The Month-end close card (mounted on the launch-active Today view and the /month-end page) shows a 'Run with Clerk' button whenever attentionCount > 0, gated only on the ungated month-end-close query — not on any Clerk feature flag. At launch clerk_ai and clerk_actions are dark, so every click fails (the server throws 503 ACTIONS_DISABLED), and the failure toast says 'Try again shortly, or use the actions card' — advice that is doubly wrong: retrying will never work until an operator flips a flag, and the ClerkActionsCard it references is also dark at launch and renders null.
evidence: dashboard.tsx lines 758-796: the button renders on close.attentionCount > 0 with no features check; the onError toast text at lines 784-789 references 'the actions card'. layout.tsx gates every other Clerk surface on feature 'clerk_ai' (lines 125-139) and ClerkDock on features.has("clerk_ai") (line 526). releases.ts: clerk_ai and clerk_actions launchDefault: false. plan-runs.ts lines 225-231: dark flag throws DomainError ACTIONS_DISABLED 503. clerk-actions-card.tsx returns null on non-success (lines 268-275).
fix: Pass me.features into MonthEndCloseCard (or call useGetMe inside it, as MonthEnd page already does) and render the 'Run with Clerk' button and MonthlyAutomationStrip only when features includes 'clerk_ai'. Reword the non-409 toast to drop the 'actions card' reference ('Nothing was changed. Try again shortly.'). Keeps the confirmation flow intact; frontend-only.

title: Foreign-currency invoices render as naira across the whole invoice flow
problem: The invoice form lets the user pick USD/EUR/GBP (CURRENCIES in invoice-new.tsx), but every money figure in the flow is formatted with formatNaira: per-line totals (line-item-row.tsx ~line 172), the Net/VAT/Total compliance sidebar (invoice-new.tsx ~lines 788-802), the vault list grandTotal (invoices.tsx ~line 719), and the detail page's unit prices, line totals and grand total (invoice-detail.tsx ~lines 1826-1839). A $1,000 invoice displays as ₦1,000.00 — off by the FX rate on a consequential financial document. The vault's min/max amount filters (invoices.tsx ~lines 530-541) also compare naira input against foreign grandTotals.
evidence: lib/format/src/index.ts already exports formatAmount(value, currency) (line 68) with the explicit comment 'so a foreign-currency figure never masquerades as naira', and the same app already uses it in dashboard.tsx, bills.tsx, obligations.tsx, recurring.tsx and clerk-actions-card.tsx — but none of the four invoice-lifecycle surfaces do; they all import only formatNaira.
fix: Swap formatNaira for the existing formatAmount(value, currency) at the cited call sites: pass draft.currency into LineItemRow/lineTotals rendering and the sidebar on invoice-new, and inv.currency / invoice.currency on the vault list and detail page. Optionally note '₦ amounts' next to the min/max filters or skip them for non-NGN rows.

title: Draft validation errors vanish into a toast and drafts have no edit path
problem: When 'Submit for stamping' fails server-side validation on a draft, the only feedback is a transient destructive toast showing just the first error (invoice-detail.tsx handleSubmit ~lines 962-970: res.errors[0]?.message). The invoice stays 'draft', and the detail page offers no way to correct it: the 'Fix & resubmit' form is rendered only inside the tone === 'failed' card (~lines 1502, 1759-1770), so a draft with a bad line, date or number cannot be edited at all — the user's only options are Cancel or 'New from this invoice'. The bulk-submit dialog makes this worse: it lists invalid drafts with only their first error and links to the detail page (invoices.tsx ~lines 245-274), where no trace of those errors exists.
evidence: invoice-detail.tsx: openFix is invoked only from the button inside the failed-submission card; useUpdateInvoice (PATCH) is already wired but only used in handleFixResubmit. There is no card or persistent list rendering validate's res.errors for draft/validated invoices.
fix: Reuse the existing fix form for draft/validated invoices (render the openFix button next to 'Submit for stamping' when status is draft/validated), and persist validate's full error list in component state rendered as a card (same row pattern as BulkSubmitDialog's 'Needs attention' list) instead of toasting only errors[0].

title: TIN-less customer hard-blocks invoice creation with no in-app remedy
problem: AddCustomerDialog labels TIN '(optional)' (add-customer-dialog.tsx line 106), and BuyerSelectOptions happily offers '(no TIN)' customers — but invoice-new.tsx makes a missing buyer TIN a blocking error (lines 258-259 set errors.buyerTin, which makes isValid false and submit() return at line 290), so the user cannot even save a DRAFT. The guidance copy contradicts the behavior ('Add the customer's Tax Identification Number before submitting' — but the block fires at creation, not submission), and there is no way to fix it: the SME app has no customers page and never calls useUpdateParty (the generated hook exists in lib/api-client-react but is unused), so the message tells the user to add a TIN with nowhere to do so.
evidence: grep for useUpdateParty in artifacts/sme-compliance/src returns nothing; the pages directory has no customers/parties route. The checklist item 'Customer has a TIN' (invoice-new.tsx line 345) stays unchecked forever for such buyers.
fix: Stop counting buyerTin in the blocking error set (keep the amber warning and the unchecked checklist item — the server enforces TIN at validation/submission), and add a small 'Add TIN' affordance next to the warning that opens a minimal edit dialog built on the AddCustomerDialog pattern using the existing useUpdateParty hook.

title: 'Draft saved offline' misstates sessionStorage lifetime; restore is silent
problem: The autosave writes to sessionStorage (invoice-new.tsx line 238), which dies when the tab closes — yet the indicator shows a Cloud icon with 'Draft saved offline' (lines 367-371), implying durable device/cloud persistence. An SME who half-finishes an invoice, trusts that message, and closes the tab (routine on mobile) loses everything. Restoration is also invisible: loadDraft silently merges a stored draft into the form (lines 106-117, 144-149) with no 'draft restored' notice, and because savedAt starts null, the entire indicator — including the only 'Discard draft' button — is hidden until the user types a keystroke (lines 366-382). Nothing on /invoices hints a resumable draft exists.
evidence: sessionStorage.setItem(draftKey, ...) at invoice-new.tsx line 238; the sign-out sweeps already anticipate localStorage drafts — landing/App.tsx lines 1301-1308 clears 'meridianiq:invoice-draft*' from BOTH localStorage and sessionStorage, while layout.tsx lines 345-350 clears sessionStorage only.
fix: Move the autosave to localStorage under the same user/firm-scoped key (layout.tsx's sign-out sweep already has the loop — extend it to localStorage like landing already does), change the copy to 'Draft saved on this device' without the Cloud icon, show the indicator + Discard button whenever a stored draft was loaded (set savedAt on restore), and add a small 'Resume draft' link on the vault header when a non-empty draft exists (reuse invoice-detail's storedDraftHasWork()).

title: Naive comma-split CSV parser corrupts quoted fields on the invoice import
problem: parseCsv in import-parse.ts (lines 51-66) splits every line with line.split(",") and ignores RFC-4180 quoting. Any CSV exported from Excel/Sheets quotes fields containing commas (buyer names like "Adaeze Foods, Ltd", descriptions like "Consulting, advisory"), so all subsequent columns shift right: dates land in TIN, numbers land in vatRate. The user sees a wall of baffling per-row errors ("Issue date is not a valid date", "Quantity must be a number") on a file that looks perfectly fine in Excel, with no hint the commas are the cause. The console's client-import.tsx (lines 47-87) already contains a correct minimal RFC-4180 parser with a comment explaining exactly this failure mode — the launch-active SME page never got it.
evidence: import-parse.ts line 59: `const cells = line.split(",");` with no quote handling. client-import.tsx lines 47-48 comment: "practice-management exports quote fields that contain commas (addresses, legal names), so a naive split(\",\") corrupts them" followed by parseCsvTable, which is not shared with or used by the SME import.
fix: Lift parseCsvTable from artifacts/console/src/pages/client-import.tsx into a shared helper (lib/web-ui or a new export in import-parse.ts) and use it in parseCsv instead of split(","). Behaviour for unquoted input is identical, so existing tests in import-parse.test.ts extend rather than change.

title: Commit is allowed without validating first, and the success toast hides skipped rows
problem: "Import valid rows" is enabled as soon as rows exist (import.tsx lines 255-261); the skip-invalid confirm dialog only fires when a PREVIOUS validation run recorded invalid rows (knownInvalidCount, lines 161-170). A user who uploads and clicks Import directly gets invalid rows silently dropped, and the completion toast (lines 140-143) says only "N invoice(s) created" — if they uploaded 50 rows and 12 were skipped, nothing above the fold says so. The console's client-import.tsx gates commit behind a validation pass (button disabled until `result && !result.committed`, lines 356-368, with the helper text "Validate first — commit unlocks after a validation pass"), so the two import surfaces teach opposite habits.
evidence: import.tsx line 162: `result && !result.committed ? result.invalidCount : 0` — knownInvalidCount is 0 when the user never validated, so onCommitClick (164-170) goes straight to run(true). The commit toast omits res.invalidCount entirely while the validation toast reports it.
fix: Mirror the console pattern: disable the commit button until a validation result exists for the current rows (result is already cleared on any edit/upload, so the gate is sound), keep the existing helper text component, and include the skipped count in the commit toast when res.invalidCount > 0 ("38 created, 12 skipped — see results below").

title: Client-detail tabs ignore launch flags: blank Money/Clerk panes, error cards under Tax & filings
problem: The client workspace's segmented control always shows all six views (today/invoices/money/compliance/clerk/setup) regardless of Me.features, while the sidebar carefully hides dark surfaces. At launch (collection_accounts, statutory_desks, client_reports, clerk_ai all dark) the Money and Clerk tabs render completely empty panes because every member card self-gates to null, and Tax & filings renders two inline 'could not load' QueryError cards (Obligations, Filings) plus a Compliance-pack card whose Download/Notify buttons hit a dark endpoint. An accountant clicking through a client sees what looks like a broken product.
evidence: client-detail.tsx: CLIENT_VIEWS (lines 85-93) and the views array (697-708) are static with no me.features check anywhere in the file. view==='money' renders only CollectionAccountsCard (returns null unless query.isSuccess, line 401) and WhtCard (returns null at wht-card.tsx:129,136 — also null for a lit firm with no WHT rows, so Money is blank even post-launch for fresh clients). view==='compliance' renders CompliancePackCard unconditionally (180-259) plus ObligationsCard/FilingsCard, which show inline QueryError on any failure (filings-card.tsx:189-193, obligations-card.tsx:538-542). Contrast layout.tsx:69-75,341-348 where nav links carry a `feature` gate precisely so users never 'navigate into a dead page'.
fix: Filter the views array by me.features using the same feature keys the nav uses (money → collection_accounts/statutory_desks, clerk → clerk_ai, compliance pack pieces → client_reports/statutory_desks), mirroring layout.tsx's NavLink.feature pattern; for a lit-but-empty Money view, render the existing EmptyState component ('Nothing to reconcile yet') instead of a bare grid.

title: 'Send invitation' implies the invitee gets an email; nothing is ever sent
problem: The submit button reads 'Send invitation' and the adjacent helper says 'They get a one-time link to set a password and join your firm' — both imply the platform delivers something to the invitee. In reality creation only returns a token; the amber card with the accept link is the sole delivery vehicle, it is shown once, and it is dismissible via an X with no confirmation and no resend path. An admin who clicks Send, sees the success toast, and moves on (or dismisses the card) has an invite stuck 'Pending' that the invitee will never receive — the only recovery is noticing weeks later and revoking/recreating.
evidence: invitations.tsx:517-527 — button text 'Send invitation' / '{create.isPending ? "Sending…" : …}' and helper 'They get a one-time link…'. submit() (149-192) only setCreated(result) client-side; no send occurs. The one-time card (623-706) carries button-dismiss-token (635-643) that discards the link instantly. The list (708-816) offers only Revoke on pending rows — no resend/regenerate.
fix: Rename the button and states to 'Create invite link' / 'Creating…', change the helper to 'MeridianIQ does not email the invite — you copy the one-time link and share it yourself', and require an explicit acknowledgement to dismiss the token card (reuse the existing amber-card copy pattern: 'Copied it? This link cannot be shown again'). Add a 'Create a new link' shortcut on pending rows that revokes and re-opens the form prefilled.

title: Zero-client empty state promotes a launch-dark import page over the working Add-client path
problem: The first-run portfolio empty state ('Import your client book') offers two CTAs: 'Bulk import clients' → /clients/import and 'Open the onboarding pipeline'. The import button is gated only on the clients.import capability, but the nav gates the same page on the white_label feature flag — dark at launch — so at launch the promoted primary button navigates into a dead page whose API 404s (exactly what the nav gating comment says it exists to prevent). The one path that works day one — the Add client dialog — is never mentioned in the empty-state body; it hides as an outline button in the header.
evidence: portfolio.tsx:1902 `canImport = (me?.capabilities ?? []).includes("clients.import")` — capability only, no features check; empty state at 2176-2206 renders button-empty-import (primary, asChild → /clients/import) and button-empty-pipeline; header Import button 1876-1884. layout.tsx:94-100 gates the /clients/import nav link with `feature: "white_label"`, and 69-75 documents why ('the API answers 404, so the link is hidden rather than navigating into a dead page'). AddClientDialog exists and is wired (2016-2019).
fix: Include the feature check in canImport (`me?.features?.includes("white_label")`, same key as layout.tsx) so both import buttons hide at launch, and make 'Add your first client' (opening the existing AddClientDialog via openAddClient) the primary CTA inside the EmptyState, with the pipeline link secondary.

title: 'Close without completing' an onboarding run is one unconfirmed click and irreversible in the UI
problem: The abandon button fires the mutation immediately — no dialog, no undo — and once the run is abandoned the card is a permanent dead end: pickOnboardingRun returns the abandoned run (no active one exists), the 'Start onboarding' button only renders in the no-run branch, and the Re-check/skip controls are gated to active runs. One slip on a ghost button sitting directly under the checklist permanently freezes the client's Setup tab at 'Closed' with no way to reopen or restart onboarding from the console.
evidence: onboarding-card.tsx:470-480 — `onClick={() => abandon.mutate({ id: run.id })}` with no confirmation. pickOnboardingRun (72-76) returns `runs.find(active) ?? runs[0]`, so an abandoned run occupies the card; the create/'Start onboarding' button lives only in the `!run` branch (269-290); status renders the 'Closed' pill (296-309) and every action button checks `run.status === "active"` (244, 352-354, 470).
fix: Wrap abandon in the existing Dialog confirm pattern (client-detail's offboard dialog is the house style) with copy stating the run closes and its checklist freezes; and when the picked run's status is 'abandoned', also render the 'Start onboarding' button so a new run can begin (the list endpoint already returns multiple runs).

title: Month-end Review buttons route to the wrong page for most checks
problem: On the launch-active /month-end page, each attention item gets a Review button whose destination is guessed by keyword regex against the item key, and the guess is wrong for 6 of the 10 checklist keys, sending users to unrelated or feature-dark pages instead of the surface that resolves the blocker.
evidence: month-end.tsx destinationFor() tests item.key with /receiv|chase|credit|cash/ -> /collections, /bill|payable/ -> /bills, /reconcil|statement/ -> /reconciliation, /vat|filing|tax/ -> /filings, else /invoices. The server's keys (month-end-close.ts lines 104-211) are overdue_submissions, unbilled_income, unmatched_credits, missing_bills, double_payments, unmatched_collections, open_obligations, open_filings, wht_credits, pending_approvals. So wht_credits and unmatched_credits match 'credit' -> /collections (should be /wht and /reconciliation), unbilled_income matches 'bill' -> /bills (a payables page, feature-dark at launch, for an item about raising invoices), and open_obligations, unmatched_collections and double_payments all fall through to /invoices (should be /obligations, /collections, /bills).
fix: Replace the regex with an explicit Record<string, string> keyed by the contract's item keys (overdue_submissions -> /invoices, unbilled_income -> /invoices/new, unmatched_credits -> /reconciliation, missing_bills and double_payments -> /bills, unmatched_collections -> /collections, open_obligations -> /obligations, open_filings -> /filings, wht_credits -> /wht, pending_approvals -> /invoices, fallback /invoices), and omit the Review button when the destination's feature flag is absent from Me.features — the same feature set layout.tsx already builds for nav gating.

title: Deadline countdowns ignore the Lagos statutory clock
area: SME calendar and dashboard deadline cards
problem: Statutory deadlines are Lagos-midnight instants server-side, but the calendar's countdown and dates render in the browser's timezone with wall-clock rounding, so the countdown contradicts the printed date on the eve of every deadline and a non-Lagos browser shows the due date one day early. Nowhere on the calendar, VAT page or dashboard is the Lagos/WAT basis stated.
evidence: calendar.tsx daysAway() does Math.round((due - Date.now()) / 86400000): a VAT deadline at Lagos midnight of the 21st (dashboard.ts line 102, lagosMidnightFor -> '...T23:00:00Z') shows the badge 'Due today' next to 'Due 21 Sept' from 12:00 Lagos on the 20th (diff 11h rounds to 0). lib/format DATE_FORMAT/DATE_TIME_FORMAT (lines 38-50) are built without a timeZone, so a UTC-browser user sees 'Due 20 Sept' for that same instant. The dashboard's Next-deadline card (dashboard.tsx line 1756) uses the same formatDate with no countdown at all, and no page mentions the timezone.
fix: Add a Lagos-pinned formatter to lib/format (a DATE_FORMAT twin with timeZone: 'Africa/Lagos') and use it for deadline dueDates on calendar.tsx and the dashboard deadline card; recompute daysAway from Lagos calendar-day difference (compare Lagos date strings, not raw ms) so the badge and the printed date always agree; and state the basis once in the calendar PageHeader description, e.g. 'Deadlines run on the Lagos (WAT) statutory calendar.'

title: Command menu is an aria-modal dialog with no focus trap and Escape only works from the search input
problem: The hand-rolled CommandMenu declares role="dialog" aria-modal="true" but implements no focus trap and no inert/aria-hidden on the page behind it, so Tab walks out of the modal into invisible background content; Escape is handled only in the input's onKeyDown, so once focus is on the Esc button or a result option, Escape does nothing and the only keyboard exits are Ctrl+K or tabbing back to the close button.
evidence: lib/web-ui/src/workspace.tsx: the global keydown listener (lines 312-322) handles only Ctrl/Cmd+K; Escape is handled solely in handleInputKeyDown on the <input> (lines 343-347). The dialog markup (lines 368-455) sets aria-modal="true" (line 379) but contains no Tab interception, no focus sentinel, and never marks sibling content inert — unlike ui/dialog.tsx and ui/sheet.tsx, which get trapping from Radix DialogPrimitive. Both lit app layouts mount it as the primary Ctrl+K navigator (sme layout.tsx lines 399-405, console layout.tsx lines 487-493).
fix: In CommandMenu, move the Escape handler up to the backdrop container (onKeyDown on the mi-command-backdrop div calling hide()) so it fires regardless of which child has focus, and add a minimal Tab cycle: onKeyDown capture Tab, collect focusable elements inside the section ref, and wrap first/last. Alternatively re-host the existing markup inside the already-shipped Radix Dialog primitive (ui/dialog.tsx pattern) and let Radix provide trap + Escape + outside-inert for free.

title: Consent revoke fires instantly with no confirmation
problem: A single click on the 'Revoke' button immediately revokes a consent layer. Layer 1 powers submission, vault and alerts; the success toast itself says 'Revocation takes effect immediately — dependent features stop within a minute.' The ledger is append-only ('never edits'), so a misclick both halts the client's compliance features and permanently records a revocation event. The same app requires an AlertDialog confirm merely to replace a local sessionStorage draft (invoice-detail.tsx line 1419).
evidence: consent.tsx lines 139-164: act() calls record.mutate directly from the button onClick (lines 231-242: onClick={() => act(l.layer, l.scope, "revoke")}) with no dialog. onError (lines 159-160) is a title-only toast 'Could not record consent' with no server reason.
fix: Wrap the revoke path in the existing shadcn AlertDialog pattern (copy artifacts/sme-compliance/src/pages/invoice-detail.tsx lines 1419-1442): title 'Revoke Layer 1 · Compliance & submission?', description restating that dependent features stop within a minute and the revocation is a permanent ledger event, destructive action button. Grant can stay one-click. Also pass serverErrorMessage(e) into the onError toast description.

title: Submit-for-stamping validation errors vanish in a 5s toast, first error only
problem: When a draft fails validation on 'Submit for stamping', the only feedback is a transient destructive toast showing res.errors[0]?.message. The remaining errors are discarded, and once the toast auto-closes (Radix default ~5s) the page looks exactly as before — the 'Submission failed' card only renders for rail rejections (tone === 'failed'), not client-side validation, and the fix form only opens for failed invoices. A user with three problems must submit three times to discover them, or is left with no trace at all.
evidence: invoice-detail.tsx lines 960-971: `const res = await validate.mutateAsync({ id }); if (!res.ok) { refreshInvoiceState(); toast({ title: "Validation failed", description: res.errors[0]?.message || "Fix the issues and try again.", variant: "destructive" }); return; }` — res.errors is never rendered anywhere on the page. Contrast the bulk-submit dialog on invoices.tsx (lines 241-277) and import.tsx results card (lines 311-343), which both list every error persistently.
fix: Hold the failed ValidationResult in component state (e.g. setValidationErrors(res.errors)) and render a persistent destructive Alert/card above the line items listing all field+message pairs — reuse the existing failed-submission card layout and FieldError styling; clear it on the next submit or edit. Keep the toast if desired.

title: Operator feature-flag Switch darkens live surfaces platform-wide with no confirm
problem: Flipping a flag Switch off immediately makes that surface's routes answer 404 for every firm — the toast copy confirms 'The surface is dark again (routes answer 404).' A stray click on the Switch (a control with no press-and-confirm affordance) takes down a live launch surface such as invoice_lifecycle for all tenants; the only feedback is a toast that auto-dismisses. There is no confirmation in either direction, unlike every other consequential action in the console (parties split, client offboard).

title: Foreign-currency invoices render as naira in the vault and invoice detail

title: Landing page offers no path for visitors without an account
problem: Every conversion CTA on the launch-active marketing page assumes an existing account. The hero ('Sign in to MeridianIQ'), the header/mobile nav ('Sign in'), the closing CTA band ('Sign in'), the footer ('Sign in'), and both live workspace cards ('Sign in to open') all point at /login. evidence: LandingPage.tsx: data-testid link-hero-login (line ~984), link-header-login (~331), link-cta-login (~1415), footer 'Sign in' (~1463); WORKSPACES entries for SME and Console both use href '/login', cta 'Sign in to open' (~96-108). title: Filing cockpit cells hide which returns are overdue
problem: The firm-wide matrix answers 'who has filed, who hasn't' but not 'who is late': an unfiled return past its statutory date still renders as slate 'Upcoming', identical to a return with weeks of runway. Overdue exists only as a footer total ('N overdue'), so a partner cannot see which client or which return is overdue without cross-checking three due dates against every row — and the per-client filings-card beside it does paint overdue red, so the two surfaces disagree.
evidence: FilingMatrixRow (openapi.yaml lines 13440-13451) only carries upcoming/prepared/filed/null per cell while the payload includes dueDates per kind and totals.overdue; matrixCellClass/matrixCellLabel in filing-matrix-card.tsx (lines 35-83) never consult dueDates, so an overdue cell gets 'Upcoming' in text-slate-600. filings-card.tsx already ships the exact pattern (filingOverdue + filingPill, lines 50-78) that overrides to a red 'Overdue' pill using localDayIso.

title: Console Ask Clerk swallows every error silently
problem: When an ask fails on the console's primary Q&A page (kill switch 503, monthly budget 429, network error), nothing visible happens: the button returns from 'Checking the register…' to 'Ask' and the previous answer (or blank space) stays on screen. The operator cannot tell whether the question was answered, refused, or lost, and never learns Clerk is switched off or the allowance is exhausted.
evidence: In ClerkAskPage (artifacts/console/src/pages/clerk-ask.tsx lines 446-448), onError only runs setAnswer(prev => heldAnswer(prev, {type:'error'})) — which by design keeps the previous answer. No toast, no banner, no inline message; AskPanel (lines 467-548) has no error prop and renders no failure state; the page imports neither useToast nor ClerkDisabledBanner, even though clerk-shell.tsx exports ClerkDisabledBanner (lines 173-183) and the sibling SME page routes the identical mutation's errors through handleClerkGatewayError (sme clerk-ask.tsx lines 517-523: 503 raises the banner, everything else toasts the server's words).
fix: Mirror the SME split on this page: in onError call killSwitchTripped(err) to set a disabledBanner state that renders the existing ClerkDisabledBanner from @/components/clerk-shell, and otherwise show the server's message — either via the console's serverErrorToast helper (already used in clerk.tsx) or an inline destructive line added to AskPanel via a new optional error prop.

title: Ask action approvals omit why, client, truncation, and draft semantics
problem: The 'Approve & run (N)' block under an Ask action proposal executes on one click without stating what it covers. The server sends why, clientName, targetCount and truncated on every AskSectionAction, but none are rendered: a truncated proposal (invoiceIds capped at 50 of e.g. 62 targets) is approved as if it covered everything, leaving the rest unhandled while the user believes the matter is closed — a compliance exposure for submit_overdue. And for draft_chasers the outcome reads 'N of N ran', implying chasers were sent when only drafts were prepared.
evidence: SectionActionApproval renders only `Approve & run (${action.invoiceIds.length})` and an outcome line saying 'ran' (sme clerk-ask.tsx lines 181-212; console clerk-ask.tsx lines 126-161). AskSectionAction carries why, clientName, targetCount, truncated (lib/api-client-react/src/generated/api.schemas.ts lines 3900-3918) — all unused in Ask, while the same repo's actions card renders action.why and a truncation note and gates execution behind a 'Review & approve' dialog listing targets (sme clerk-actions-card.tsx lines 305-347), and the mobile lib phrases truncation explicitly (artifacts/mobile/lib/automation.ts line 96). PlanRunProgress knows drafts need review ('drafted — review before submitting', console clerk-ask.tsx line 54) but the single-section outcome does not.
fix: Render action.why and clientName above the button; when action.truncated, add the existing mobile copy pattern ('covers the oldest {invoiceIds.length} of {targetCount} — approve, then come back for the rest'); make the label and outcome kind-aware for draft_chasers ('Prepare N chaser drafts' / 'N drafts prepared — review before sending'). Optionally reuse the actions-card confirm-dialog pattern so Ask approvals match that surface's two-step consent.

title: SME batch progress and failures vanish after leaving the page
problem: The batch progress alert promises 'you can leave this page; the work continues', but the batch id lives only in component state. A client who leaves and returns sees no trace of a queued or processing bundle, and if the bundle fails after they leave (a failed batch creates no cases), the failure is never surfaced anywhere — the invoices they believe they sent silently never appear.
evidence: clerk-capture.tsx line 663 renders ' — you can leave this page; the work continues.'; activeBatchId is useState (line 265) set only in createBatch.onSuccess (line 355) and the only batch query is useGetClerkBatch by that held id (lines 363-372). failReason renders only in the mounted alert (lines 643-646). No useListClerkBatches call exists anywhere in sme-compliance (grep returns nothing), though the hook exists and the console uses it (console clerk.tsx line 1690).
fix: On mount, query useListClerkBatches and rehydrate: if any batch is queued/processing, restore the existing progress Alert (re-using the current activeBatch rendering by setting activeBatchId); if the most recent batch failed and created no cases, show the same destructive Alert with its failReason so the failure survives navigation.

title: Bulk-confirm dialog omits the consequences the single flow states
problem: Confirming a single invoice shows RESPONSE_DESCRIPTIONS.confirmed ('Accepts the invoice as issued. The supplier is notified, and with the no-set-off acknowledgement… the invoice becomes financeable') plus 'Confirming without set-off makes this invoice financeable.' The bulk path — up to 50 invoices at once — asks only 'Confirm N invoices?' / 'Each records who confirmed and how, permanently.' The dialog states neither the total Naira value being confirmed, nor that suppliers are notified, nor whether the no-set-off acknowledgement (ticked or not in the bar behind the dialog) is being applied to every one of the N invoices and what that makes them (financeable). The buyer's largest single action carries the thinnest consequence statement in the app.
evidence: confirmations.tsx AlertDialog ~728-751: title 'Confirm {selected.size} invoices?', description 'Each records who confirmed and how, permanently.' The bulk noSetOff checkbox (~696-711) has no financeability hint, unlike invoice-respond.tsx ~532-534. The selected set's total value is computable client-side (grandTotal is on every BuyerInvoice in `invoices`), but never shown.

Suppliers are notified{bulkNoSetOff ? ', and with your no-set-off acknowledgement these invoices become financeable' : ''}. Each response is recorded permanently.' Reuse the existing dialog — do not add steps.

title: Invite/reset token is stripped from the URL on load, so a refresh shows a misleading 'missing token' dead end; expired-invite errors also lack a next step
problem: takeQuerySecret deletes the token from the URL via history.replaceState the moment the page mounts. If the invitee refreshes (or the browser restores the tab after a network hiccup), the page shows "Invitation link incomplete… Ask your administrator to resend it" — escalating to an admin when simply re-opening the original email link would have worked. Separately, an actually-expired invite is only discovered AFTER the user has filled in name + password + confirm, and that 400 message offers no recovery action at all.
evidence: query-secret.ts lines 6-14 delete the token and replaceState immediately; AcceptInvite.tsx line 70 captures it once in useState, so any reload yields token=null and the card at lines 105-127 ("missing its token… Ask your administrator to resend it"). ResetPassword.tsx has the identical pattern (line 51, guidance card lines 76-102). The 400 branch in acceptError (AcceptInvite.tsx lines 16-21) returns only "This invitation link is invalid or has expired." with showSignIn:false — no resend guidance, unlike the missing-token card — and it is shown only after submit.
fix: Keep the URL-stripping (it is a deliberate log-hygiene control) but make takeQuerySecret stash the value in sessionStorage under a page-scoped key and read it back on a later mount in the same tab, so refresh survives. Content fixes: on the missing-token cards add "If you refreshed this page, open the link from your invitation/reset email again — it still works until it is redeemed"; add "Ask your administrator to send a fresh invitation." to the 400 acceptError message.

title: 'Forgot your password?' ends at a card with no contact path and no answer for firm admins
problem: There is no self-serve reset (by design), so a locked-out user's only path is the guidance card — but it names "your firm administrator — or MeridianIQ support" without any link, email address, or button to reach either, and it says nothing to the firm_admin who IS the administrator and has no one above them in-product.
evidence: The sign-in form's "Forgot your password?" link (App.tsx lines 575-581) goes to /reset-password, whose token-less branch (ResetPassword.tsx lines 76-102) renders two sentences of prose and a single "Back to sign in" button. No mailto:, no support URL, no distinction by audience — a locked-out user cannot act on the instruction from this screen, and the most locked-out persona (firm admin) gets advice that cannot apply to them.
fix: Add a second Button (variant="outline", asChild) with a mailto: support address or the marketing site's contact page, and split the copy into two lines: "Client and staff accounts: ask your firm administrator for a reset link." / "Firm administrators and buyers: contact MeridianIQ support." Pure content + one anchor; no flow change.

title: Console's wrong-workspace card uses raw role jargon and routes the user to the portal instead of their own app
problem: A client_user who lands on /console (bookmark, shared link) gets a card that leans on internal RBAC vocabulary — "You are signed in as client user. This console requires a firm admin or operator or firm staff or auditor account" — and its only action is an extra hop back to the portal, rather than a direct button to the workspace that account can actually use.

The only CTA is "Back to the MeridianIQ portal" (lines 135-142); the SME app's equivalent card (sme require-session.tsx lines 112-133) has the same portal-only CTA.

Mirror the deep-link in the SME card.

title: Clerk dashboard tab is visible at launch and permanently empty (capability-only gate, unlike the nav)
problem: The dashboard adds a 'Clerk' tab whenever the principal holds the clerk.ask capability, with no feature-flag check — but client_user holds clerk.ask (it was widened for Ask Clerk), and at launch clerk_ai is dark. So every launch user sees a 'Clerk' tab whose two possible cards both render null: ClerkDigestCard (the digest route refuses client_user explicitly, and is flag-dark for firm users) and ClerkActionsCard (clerk_actions dark). Clicking the tab yields a blank pane, while the sidebar correctly hides all Clerk links behind the clerk_ai feature — the two gates disagree on the same screen.
evidence: dashboard.tsx line 1482: canAskClerk = !!me?.capabilities.includes("clerk.ask") (no features check), tab pushed at lines 1615-1617; ClerkDigestCard returns null on non-success (lines 445-448, comment says the digest is firm-only); ClerkActionsCard returns null (clerk-actions-card.tsx lines 268-275). rbac.ts line 223: client_user includes "clerk.ask", with the comment 'Firm-internal surfaces that share this capability must refuse client_user explicitly (see GET /clerk/digest)'. layout.tsx lines 125-139 gate the same surfaces on feature: "clerk_ai".

title: Month-end close checklist speaks dark-feature accountant vocabulary to launch-profile SMEs
problem: The Month-end close card renders every server-computed checklist line regardless of the launch profile, so a launch SME's Today view lists ~9 rows including 'Statutory returns', 'WHT credit notes', 'Authority obligations', 'Bank credits with no invoice', 'Collection-account payments matching no invoice' and 'Expected vendor bills not captured' — all checks for desks (statutory_desks, reconciliation, collection_accounts, money_analytics) that are launch-dark and whose nav links the sidebar deliberately hides. A new business owner reads a wall of jargon about features they cannot reach anywhere in the app, on the largest card of the launch landing view.
evidence: month-end-close.ts lines 104-209 build the fixed item list (keys open_filings, wht_credits, open_obligations, unmatched_credits, unmatched_collections, missing_bills, double_payments) with no feature filtering; dashboard.tsx MonthEndCloseCard maps close.items unfiltered (lines 720-757) and is mounted unconditionally in the today view (lines 1773-1775). releases.ts: statutory_desks, money_analytics, collection_accounts, reconciliation all launchDefault: false; layout.tsx hides the corresponding nav links via feature gates (lines 67-119).
fix: Frontend-only filter: define a key→feature map in the card (open_filings/wht_credits/open_obligations → statutory_desks; missing_bills/double_payments → money_analytics; unmatched_credits → reconciliation; unmatched_collections → collection_accounts) and drop items whose feature is absent from me.features, deriving the shown attention/clear counts from the filtered list. Launch users then see only the invoice-core checks (overdue submissions, unbilled income, pending approvals).

title: Month-end 'Review' buttons deep-link by fragile regex into wrong or nav-hidden destinations
problem: The launch-active /month-end page routes each attention item via destinationFor(), a regex over the item key. The mapping is wrong for several real keys: 'wht_credits' matches /credit/ and sends the user to /collections instead of /wht; 'open_obligations' matches nothing and falls through to /invoices instead of /obligations; 'double_payments' and 'unmatched_collections' also land on /invoices. And every mapped destination except /invoices (/collections, /bills, /reconciliation, /filings) is a launch-dark surface the sidebar hides — the user arrives on a page with no active nav highlight, and /filings (unlike reconciliation and b2c, the only pages using FeatureUnavailable) answers a dark flag with a destructive 'Unable to load … Try again' error whose retry can never succeed.
evidence: month-end.tsx lines 27-33: destinationFor tests /receiv|chase|credit|cash/ → /collections, /bill|payable/ → /bills, /reconcil|statement/ → /reconciliation, /vat|filing|tax/ → /filings, else /invoices. Real keys from month-end-close.ts (lines 104-209) include wht_credits, open_obligations, double_payments, unmatched_collections. App.tsx routes all these paths unconditionally (lines 55-71). Grep shows only reconciliation.tsx and b2c.tsx import FeatureUnavailable; filings.tsx uses QueryError on failure.
fix: Replace the regex with an exact key→href map (wht_credits → /wht, open_obligations → /obligations, missing_bills/double_payments → /bills, unmatched_collections → /collections, open_filings → /filings, default /invoices), and only render the Review button when the destination's feature is present in me.features (fall back to no button, matching the sidebar's PL-02 gate). Pairs naturally with the checklist feature filter.

title: Alert settings invites configuring WhatsApp/SMS/email delivery that is launch-dark, with unexplained 'Send failed' test results
problem: The sidebar shows 'Alert settings' with no feature gate while the messaging rail (messaging_notifications) is launch-dark. A launch user can enable WhatsApp/SMS/email channels, enter numbers, and press the test-send button — every channel comes back as a failed row with the generic detail 'Send failed', with nothing telling them the platform's outbound messaging simply is not switched on yet. They will debug their phone number instead of learning the truth, and will trust alerts that never arrive.
evidence: layout.tsx line 147: { href: "/alerts", label: "Alert settings", icon: Bell } has no feature attribute, unlike the surrounding gated links (the file's own comment at lines 49-52 says absent features mean dead pages should be hidden). releases.ts: messaging_notifications launchDefault: false. alerts.tsx renders the full channel form and useSendTestAlert. alert-prefs.ts lines 148-158: any send exception is caught and returned as { status: "failed", detail: "Send failed" }.
fix: Add feature: "messaging_notifications" to the Alert settings nav link, and on the page itself (still reachable by URL) show an informational banner when me.features lacks messaging_notifications — reuse the FeatureUnavailable card ('Alerts are not yet enabled…') above the form instead of letting test sends fail opaquely. No backend change.

title: Post-submit copy promises notifications that are dark at launch; pending state never refreshes
problem: Both success toasts after submission say "We'll notify you once it clears the rail" (handleSubmit ~lines 975-978 and handleFixResubmit ~lines 1042-1044), but messaging_notifications is launch-dark, so at launch no notification will ever arrive — the user waits for a ping that never comes. Meanwhile the page gives no persistent 'what happens next' for the submitted state: the toast disappears in seconds, useGetInvoice has no refetchInterval (~lines 831-833), so a 'Pending stamp' invoice never advances to Stamped on screen without a manual reload, and the only durable cue is the timeline row 'Attempt 1 · Pending'.
evidence: Launch profile R62 lists messaging_notifications as staged/dark; the detail page has no polling and no pending-state explainer card (ComplianceStatusCard is progressive enhancement that renders nothing on fetch failure).
fix: Gate the toast copy on me.features (already available via useGetMe — layout filters nav with it): when messaging_notifications is absent say 'Check back here — the status on this page updates when FIRS answers.' Add refetchInterval (e.g. 15-30s while invoice.status === 'submitted') to useGetInvoice and the attempts query so the pending state resolves on screen.

title: Vault filter tabs use different vocabulary than badges and omit three statuses
problem: The filter pills are All / Unsubmitted / Pending / Stamped / Failed (invoices.tsx lines 57-63), but the row badges say Draft, Validated, Pending stamp, Stamped, Confirmed, Settled, Credited, Cancelled (statusLabel, lib/format/src/index.ts lines 207-217). 'Unsubmitted' vs 'Draft/Validated' and 'Pending' vs 'Pending stamp' force the user to map two vocabularies, and the tone map (STATUS_TONES lines 189-199) gives settled, credited and cancelled tones no matching tab key — so a settled invoice disappears from the 'Stamped' tab it used to live in and is findable only under 'All'. Nowhere in the app is the lifecycle vocabulary explained.
evidence: countFor/rows filter with statusTone(inv.status) === key (lines 524-541); tone keys 'settled', 'credited', 'cancelled' match no FILTERS entry, so those invoices are excluded from every non-'All' tab.
fix: Align tab labels with badge words (e.g. 'Drafts', 'Pending stamp') and add a 'Settled' tab (folding credited into it or adding 'Closed' for credited+cancelled), keeping the same statusTone grouping. Add a one-line legend or info tooltip near the tabs explaining the lifecycle order (Draft → Validated → Pending stamp → Stamped → Settled).

title: Tab counts and status filters only cover loaded pages, misreading as totals
problem: The list loads 50 rows per page (PAGE_SIZE, line 67) and the tab counts are computed over only the loaded rows (countFor over scoped, lines 524-527), yet they render as bare authoritative numbers ('Failed · 0'). A user with a failed invoice on page 2 sees 'Failed · 0', clicks the tab, and gets the 'No matches' empty state (lines 677-692) whose only action is 'Clear filters' — no hint that unloaded pages may hold matches and no Load more button in that state (the load-more footer requires rows to be visible, line 733). The same applies to the date/amount filters.
evidence: hasMore (line 139) is known when counts render, but the count string `· ${countFor(f.key)}` (line 622) never reflects it; the filtered empty state and the footer both key off rows/loaded lengths that exclude unloaded pages.
fix: When hasMore is true, suffix counts with '+' (e.g. 'Failed · 0+') or hide them, and in the filtered 'No matches' empty state add the existing Load more button ('Load older invoices to keep searching') alongside Clear filters.

title: Legacy .xls is advertised in the picker but parsed as text into garbage rows with no error
problem: The file input accepts ".csv,.xlsx,.xls,...application/vnd.ms-excel" (import.tsx line 203), but isExcel matches only /\.xlsx$/i (import-parse.ts lines 88-90), so a legacy binary .xls falls into the text branch: file.text() decodes binary to mojibake, parseCsv happily maps it, and the page reports "N row(s) ready" of garbage — the catch/toast never fires because neither call throws. The in-file comment (import.tsx lines 79-82) claims "a legacy binary .xls surfaces the read-error toast", which is not what the code does. The user is told their file loaded, then drowns in nonsense validation errors with no clue the format is unsupported.
evidence: import.tsx onFile (106-127): the else branch does `setRaw(await file.text())` for anything not matching isExcel; parseCsv (import-parse.ts 51-66) never throws on binary content, so the destructive "Could not read file" toast is unreachable for .xls.
fix: Remove ".xls" and "application/vnd.ms-excel" from the accept string, and add an explicit guard in onFile: if /\.xls$/i.test(file.name), show the existing destructive toast with "Legacy .xls isn't supported — save the sheet as .xlsx or CSV and re-upload."

title: Failed rows cannot be exported for fix-and-retry; results download omits the original data
problem: After a partial import, the skip-confirm dialog promises "You can fix and re-import them later" (import.tsx lines 270-274), but the only export is downloadResults (lines 172-186), which emits rowNumber/invoiceNumber/status/errors — none of the original cell values. For an .xlsx upload the rows are also not editable in the page (the textarea stays empty; fileRows lives only in memory), so the user must reopen their spreadsheet, hunt down each failed rowNumber by hand, fix it, and re-upload the whole file — at which point the already-created rows now fail as duplicates, muddying the second run's results.
evidence: downloadResults builds `head = "rowNumber,invoiceNumber,status,errors"` only. The full original rows are available client-side in the `rows` memo (line 101-104) keyed by rowNumber, but are never joined into the export.
fix: Add a "Download failed rows (CSV)" ghost button next to the existing Download when result.invalidCount > 0: emit template-format CSV (COLUMNS header + the original row values for rows whose result status is invalid, joined via rowNumber). The user can fix just those rows and paste/upload them back, and a re-run contains no duplicates of the created rows.

title: After a committed import there is no path to the created invoices, and drafts are never mentioned
problem: On commit the toast says "N invoice(s) created" and the results card lists row statuses, but nothing on the page links to where the invoices went, and no copy says they were created as DRAFTS that still need review/submission (the server path is createDraft/bulkCreateDrafts — artifacts/api-server/src/modules/invoice/import.ts lines 150, 242). A first-time SME user finishes the flow on a dead end and may believe the invoices are already filed with FIRS — a compliance-relevant misunderstanding on this platform.
evidence: import.tsx lines 139-148 (commit toast) and 291-346 (results card): no Link/route navigation anywhere on the page besides template downloads; the word "draft" never appears in the page copy.
fix: When result.committed, add a primary "View draft invoices" button (wouter Link to the invoices route) in the results-card header, and change the toast/description to "N draft invoice(s) created — review and submit them from Invoices."

title: Validation pass gives no duplicate warning — dupes only surface after commit
problem: validateImportRow (artifacts/api-server/src/modules/invoice/import.ts lines 35-88) checks only presence/format — a file where the same invoiceNumber appears twice, or re-uses a number that already exists, validates as "all valid". The duplicate only fails at commit time as a per-row error (the comment at lines 216-218 names "duplicate invoice number" as a commit-time failure), so the user gets a green validation preview and then a partially failed import. Intra-file duplicates are fully detectable client-side before anything is sent, and the UI does nothing with that.
evidence: import.tsx renders only "{rows.length} row(s) ready" (lines 234-243); no client-side scan of rows for repeated invoiceNumber values, though the parsed rows are in memory. Console's client-import at least surfaces an "Already exist" status tile for its own dup class; the SME result schema has no equivalent status (openapi.yaml InvoiceImportRowResult enum: valid/invalid/created).
fix: Purely client-side: before enabling commit, scan `rows` for repeated invoiceNumber values and render an inline amber warning under the rows-ready line ("2 rows share invoice number INV-2001 — the second will fail on import"), reusing the destructive/muted text patterns already on the page.

title: The 5,000-row cap and format expectations are never communicated before failure
problem: The server rejects imports over MAX_IMPORT_ROWS = 5000 with a 413 (artifacts/api-server/src/routes/sme/import.ts lines 16-34), but the page shows no format or size guidance anywhere: nothing says which columns are expected (only downloading the template reveals them), that only the first sheet of an .xlsx is read, or that 5,000 rows is the ceiling. A migrating SME with a 9,000-row book uploads the whole payload, waits, and gets an error toast after the fact; the row count is known client-side (rows.length) before any request is made.
evidence: import.tsx card 1 (lines 196-245) contains only the three buttons and the textarea placeholder; run() (129-157) submits regardless of rows.length, so oversized files fail server-side with the generic toast pipeline.
fix: Add one muted helper line under the picker: "CSV or Excel (.xlsx) — first sheet, template columns, up to 5,000 rows per import." Add a client-side check: when rows.length > 5000, disable both action buttons and show an inline destructive message suggesting splitting the file.

title: No drag-and-drop target on the bulk-import surface
problem: The only way to get a file in is the small outline FilePickerButton (file-picker-button.tsx lines 20-27) — there is no dropzone, and dragging a spreadsheet onto the page does nothing (worse, the browser default navigates away from the page to the file, losing any pasted rows). Bulk import is the one surface where users arrive holding a file; a visible drop area is the expected affordance and the current card layout has room for it.
evidence: use-file-picker.ts exposes only inputProps/openPicker — no drag handlers exist anywhere in the flow; import.tsx card 1 renders buttons + textarea with no onDragOver/onDrop and no dragenter styling.
fix: Extend useFilePicker to also return dropProps ({onDragOver: preventDefault, onDrop: e => onFile(e.dataTransfer.files[0])}) and spread them on the "1. Add your rows" CardContent with a dashed-border highlight while dragging; the existing onFile handler and read-failure toast are reused unchanged, and reconciliation (the other FilePickerButton consumer) gets it for free.

title: Network failure during commit shows "Please check your file", inviting a duplicate re-import
problem: run()'s catch (import.tsx lines 150-156) shows one toast for every failure: "Import failed — <message or> Please check your file." A dropped connection mid-commit (common on the mobile networks this product targets) hits the same copy: the file is blamed although it is fine, and the user has no way to know whether the server already created the invoices (the request may have committed before the response was lost). The obvious next move — clicking "Import valid rows" again — re-submits everything; the page gives zero guidance about checking the invoice list first, and the single non-streaming POST means the only in-flight feedback for a 5,000-row import is the button label flipping to "Working…" (line 260) with no progress or skeleton (the console page at least renders a Skeleton while pending, client-import.tsx line 376).
evidence: catch (e) { toast({ title: "Import failed", description: e instanceof Error ? e.message : "Please check your file." }) } — a fetch TypeError ("Failed to fetch") surfaces raw or falls back to file-blaming copy; no offline/network branch exists, and nothing disables the textarea or shows progress during the pending mutation.
fix: In the commit catch, branch on network-shaped errors (TypeError / !navigator.onLine): show "We couldn't confirm the import — your connection dropped. Check your Invoices list before retrying to avoid duplicates" with a link to the invoices route. While importMut.isPending, render the console's Skeleton pattern under the action row and disable the textarea/picker so rows can't change mid-flight.

title: Invitations list hides which client a client-login is scoped to, and expired invites still read 'Pending'
problem: A firm admin inviting owners for several clients sees rows that are indistinguishable: the table shows Email/Role/Status/Created/Expires but never the client the login is scoped to, even though the API returns it and the portfolio (already fetched on this page for the picker) can resolve the name. Separately, the status pill is derived purely from the stored enum (pending/accepted/revoked), so an invite past its expiresAt still shows an amber 'Pending' with a live Revoke button — the admin cannot tell at a glance which pending invites are actually dead and need re-issuing.
evidence: invitations.tsx table headers 734-759 and rows 762-810 render no client column; Invitation carries clientPartyId (api.schemas.ts:121-133, line 127). The page already holds portfolio.clients (93-95, 124). invitations.ts:25-50 — invitationStatusTone/Label switch only on 'pending'/'accepted'/'revoked'; no expired handling anywhere.
fix: Add a 'Client' column that maps inv.clientPartyId to portfolio legalName (fall back to the short UUID like the operator Firm column does at 766-777), and derive an 'Expired' slate pill client-side when status==='pending' && new Date(inv.expiresAt) < now, adding the case to invitationStatusTone/Label.

title: Pipeline 'Active' stage is a dead end — no way to turn a won prospect into a client
problem: The page promises to 'Track prospects from lead to active client', and the portfolio empty state routes new firms here, but moving a prospect to Active only shows a toast — the client book is untouched and the Active column offers no 'Add as client' action, so the accountant must remember to re-type the prospect's name (and re-find the contact email, which is captured at creation but never displayed on any card afterwards) in the separate Add client dialog. evidence:

Prospect cards render only name and '~N inv/mo' (261-263) — contactEmail from the create form (161-167) is never shown or editable again (updateProspect sends stage only, line 111). Empty columns render `

—

` (250-251).

title: Getting-started checklist ships internal jargon: '(manual anchor: #consent)' and 'Layer 1 sharing consent'
problem: The consent row of the first-run Getting started card — the very first thing a new firm reads — renders literal spec/dev vocabulary to the user: '— the client signs in and grants Layer 1 sharing consent from their own workspace (manual anchor: #consent). Not tracked here.' 'Layer 1' and '(manual anchor: #consent)' are internal annotations that mean nothing to an accountant and read as a bug, undermining trust on the flagship onboarding surface.
evidence: portfolio.tsx:398-404 — the step.id === 'consent' branch renders exactly that string inside GettingStartedCard, which shows for every firm until 3 of 4 steps complete (shouldShowGettingStarted, 268-275).

title: Client book rows: name isn't a link and the whole row isn't clickable, despite hover styling
problem:
In the ClientWorkbenchTable — the accountant's main jump-off into a client — the client name is a plain

and the only navigation affordance is a small ghost 'Open' button at the far right of a 52rem-wide row, even though the row paints a teal hover wash that signals clickability. Opening 20 clients in a session means 20 precise trips to the right edge. Returning is equally lossy: client-detail's back link always goes to '/' (the Today view), discarding the clients tab, search, risk filter and sort the accountant had set (all component state, not URL params), so every switch restarts the triage.
evidence:
portfolio.tsx:1777-1791 — row has hover:bg-teal-50/40 but the name cell renders `

{client.legalName}

`; only the Actions cell (1828-1835) holds a Link. The scorecard table already links names (1299-1305), so the pattern exists on the same page. client-detail.tsx:712-718 back link is hardcoded href="/"; clientSearch/clientRisk/clientSort are useState only (1897-1899), so they are lost on navigation.

title: Penalty-risk ranking is never explained anywhere the badge appears
problem: Risk is the portfolio's default sort, its headline stat ('High-risk clients — Partner attention'), a filter, and the client header badge — yet no surface says what drives it or how to lower it. The badge is just a colored word ('High risk'), and the client-detail Metric explains it circularly as 'Current client exposure'. An accountant defending the ranking to a partner or a client has nothing to point at, and can't tell whether clearing failed submissions or overdue deadlines will move a client out of red.
evidence: format.ts:20-32 — riskLabel/riskBadgeClasses produce only `${humanize(risk)} risk` plus a tone. portfolio.tsx risk column header is the bare word 'Risk' (1768); the only hint is the Today work-item sentence 'Overdue paper or repeated failures require partner attention' (2073-2074), which never appears near the badges. client-detail.tsx:784-790 Metric label 'Penalty risk', detail 'Current client exposure'.

title: Advisory with zero clients: guidance is a dead paragraph inside a dropdown, pointing at a launch-dark page
problem: A first-run firm opening the launch-active Advisory page sees a normal-looking 'Pick the client being assessed' select; only after opening it do they find a non-interactive paragraph telling them to visit 'the Client import page' — a page that is hidden from the nav at launch (white_label feature) and cannot be linked from inside SelectContent anyway. Meanwhile the full questionnaire renders below and 'Run assessment' sits disabled with no visible reason, so the page reads as broken rather than as 'add a client first'.
evidence:
advisory.tsx:218-231 — the zero-client case renders `

No clients yet — import your client book from the Client import page first.

` inside SelectContent; the submit button disables on !clientPartyId (279-284) with only the answered-count caption beside it. layout.tsx:94-100 gates /clients/import behind feature 'white_label' (launch-dark).
